# A bank split finer than the currency: 100.005 USD.
#
# The question this fixture settles is whether the restatement can ever be
# handed a figure the receivable cannot hold. `relink_a_parked_split` copies
# the bank split's amount onto the receivable, and the receivable is kept to
# the cent; a bank kept to a tenth of one, holding 100.005, would put a figure
# there that the export then refuses — a book this tool wrote and cannot read
# back.
#
# It cannot arrive this way. A booked amount is judged against the *currency*,
# whatever unit the account is kept to, so a file may not state 100.005 in USD
# at all — the same rule `credit_on_an_account_kept_finer_than_the_cent.txt`
# records, where 50.005 was refused for putting an amount at the account's
# unit against a value at the currency's, with an invented rate between CAD
# and CAD to make the two balance.
#
# So this file is refused before any invoice sees it, and the restatement is
# unreachable with such a figure through this tool. A book GnuCash itself
# wrote that way is a different matter, which is why the guard is asked
# anyway.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the amount.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
2026-03-12 * "Money in, finer than the cent"
	guid: "c0ffee00c0ffee00c0ffee00c0ffee00"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Bank:USD 100.005 USD
		guid: "d0ffee00c0ffee00c0ffee00c0ffee01"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Suspense USD -100.005 USD
		guid: "e0ffee00c0ffee00c0ffee00c0ffee02"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
